_note: The programme, bundled into the app shell so anvil is usable on first open with no token and no network. Structure and coaching cues only: this repo is public and never carries real logged data, loads, or personal health details. The live copy lives in the private data repo and wins whenever it loads.

exercises.name: Med Ball Slam
exercises.note: Power, first, while fresh. Throw it hard, do not grind it. The only rate-of-force work in the week.

exercises.name: Back Squat
exercises.note: Primary. Leave 1-2 in reserve. Depth + control.

exercises.name: Standing Calf Raise
exercises.note: Pause + full stretch at the bottom.

exercises.name: Weighted Pull-up or Lat Pulldown
exercises.note: Builds the muscle-up. Full dead-hang stretch, chest to bar.

exercises.name: Chest-Supported Row (or DB Row)
exercises.note: Strict, pad stops cheating. Squeeze + pause.

exercises.name: Incline DB Curl
exercises.note: Arms behind torso = deep biceps stretch. Last set to failure.

exercises.name: Flat Bench or Machine Chest Press
Pull-up / Muscle-up Skill Work
exercises.note: FRESH, first: explosive pull-ups, high pulls, straight-bar dips, slow negatives.

exercises.name: Single-arm DB Row
exercises.note: Big stretch. Last set near failure.

exercises.name: Dead Hang
exercises.note: Grip + shoulder decompression. Bar, open hand, never an edge.

exercises.name: Med Ball Side Toss
exercises.note: Rotational power, first, while fresh. The transverse plane nothing else trains.

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift
exercises.note: Leave 1-2 in reserve. Hinge, feel the hamstring stretch.

exercises.name: Lateral Lunge
exercises.note: THE frontal plane, taken from Ben's sheet. You play a lateral sport and this programme trained one plane.

exercises.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
exercises.note: Single-leg strength; carries over to court and rock.

exercises.name: DB Half-Kneeling One-Arm Press
exercises.note: From Ben's sheet. A shoulder-friendlier overhead position than a loaded bilateral press.

exercises.name: Side Plank with Hip Hike
exercises.note: From Ben's sheet, and it upgrades the bodyweight version in Core. Anti-lateral-flexion, loaded.

_tiers: P3. Every session has three versions and all of them advance the rotation. An exercise's `tier` is the LOWEST tier it survives to: 3 = the one movement that still counts as having trained, 2 = the main work, 1 = accessory. Tier N shows every exercise with tier >= N. A tier 3 day is a completed day; the alternative to tier 3 is not tier 1, it is nothing.

conditioning._note: Replaces the inspiratory-muscle trainer, cancelled 2026-08-19: its one mechanism is available free from running, and the device's effect sizes shrink toward zero in trained people. Two hard sessions a week is the dose where the VO2max curve flattens (Rosenblat 2020/2022); a third buys fatigue rather than adaptation. They sit on upper-body mornings because explosive strength is the one thing concurrent training genuinely costs (Schumann 2022, SMD -0.28) and it is worst same-session with heavy lower work.
conditioning.watchRule: Apple Watch Cardio Fitness updates ONLY from Outdoor Walk, Outdoor Run and Outdoor Hike. Treadmill, gym and indoor interval work never move the number no matter how hard it was. Log at least one session a week OUTDOORS under open sky, started as an Outdoor Run, or a whole training block reads as a flat line.

tue.name: Norwegian 4x4
tue.fallback: 2 x 4 min, same intensity, one recovery between
tue.why: The most replicated interval protocol there is: ~7% VO2max in 8 weeks at 3 sessions a week, beating long slow distance, threshold work and 15/15 on the same time budget (Helgerud 2007). Long intervals are the powerful tool.
tue.progression: Weeks 4-6: 5 x 4 min if resting HR trend and lifting numbers are both holding. Weeks 10-12: back to 4 reps as the long run takes over.

thu.work: 5 x (30 s easy, 20 s moderate, 10 s near-maximal), 2-3 blocks
thu.why: Best adaptation per minute in the literature: ~4% VO2max, 1500 m down 21 s and 5 km down 48 s in 7 weeks, on about 12-18 min of actual work, in runners who were already training (Gunnarsson and Bangsbo 2012). Short intervals are the efficient tool.
thu.progression: Hold the volume, sharpen the 10 s reps toward true sprint effort.

sat.name: Alternating: sprints one week, long run the next
sat.work: Week A: 10 x 20 s near-maximal, 40 s easy. Week B: continuous easy run at 60-70% max HR
sat.recovery: Week A: 40 s between reps. Week B: none, it is the easy session
sat.fallback: Week A: 6 reps. Week B: 15 min easy
sat.why: The one session serving the half marathon rather than VO2max. Week B grows from week 7 as race specificity starts outweighing marginal VO2max, which is flattening by then anyway.

_conditioningRest: Monday and Wednesday are the heavy and technical lower days and carry no conditioning on purpose. Friday is left clear so a missed Tuesday or Thursday has somewhere to go without stacking two hard sessions back to back.
